messages:
maria: quick heads-up: canary-42 showed a stale-prefix serve after a demote->evict. trace looks like prefetch writeback resurrected the prefix after observer marked it demoted. anyone seen this pattern before?
aj: saw a variant last month. suspicious race between prefetch completion and observer applying demote tombstone. writeback had no epoch check.
ken: question: do we want writeback to be strongly guarded (CAS on prefix_meta) or introduce a lightweight tombstone check that is best-effort?
clara: strong CAS gives linearizability but costs ~1 RPC to sidecar metadata store on commit. for 99th p99 latency sensitive workloads that's nontrivial.
pavel: lightweight tombstone approach: publish tombstone_epoch when demote happens, observer broadcasts to local node, writeback aborts if tombstone_epoch > prefetch_epoch. no lock required.
aj: pseudocode for tombstone check: ```if (read_meta(prefix).tombstone_epoch > prefetch.epoch) abort_writeback(); else commit_local();``` cheap but relies on prompt propagation.
ken: propagation gap is the issue. if tombstone hasn't landed locally yet, writeback slips through. can we flip semantics: on demote, also publish a transient denylist in the local slab coordinator so local writebacks check O(1) table before commit?
clara: that's doable: observer push -> local denylist set (in-memory, expiry 2s) -> writeback looks up in-memory denylist before writing. combines speed with low overhead.
maria: ops impact? more in-memory checks per writeback. benchmark?
ops-bot: benchmark note: simulated denylist lookup added ~0.4% median CPU and +0.6ms tail on writeback path in yesterday's run. link: <internal/perf/174> :chart_with_upwards_trend: 
pavel: another variant: optimistic commit + read-time validation. allow writeback, but any read checks epoch; if stale detected, read triggers a rehydrate or fallback to remote. shifts cost to read path.
aj: that helps workloads with rare reads, but hurts hot-read tails. we need SLO-informed choice per tenant. maybe configurable policy: tenant-level strong_consistency: true/false.
ken: public API note: we must define pin semantics. if a user calls `pin(prefix)`, we should require strong_consistency (prevent demote) OR explicitly document that pin is "best-effort sticky". ambiguous semantics will cause support tickets.
clara: propose two APIs: `pin(prefix)` => hard lease (no demote until unpin); `soft_pin(prefix, ttl)` => prefer keep-warm but allow demote with tombstone. clear and mirrors current internal concepts.
maria: agree. action items: 1) implement local denylist fast-path + tombstone_epoch check on writeback (clara + pavel) 2) add tenant-level consistency flag and docs for pin vs soft_pin (ken) 3) metrics: writeback-aborts, denylist-hits, stale-reads-detected (aj) 4) plan canary and chaos test (maria)
pavel: I'll add observer hook to push denylist entries to slab coordinator; TTL default 2s, configurable per-cluster.
aj: I'll add metrics and a Grafana panel. also add an alert for stale-reads-detected > 0.1% of reads over 5m.
ken: drafting docs for pin semantics now; will include migration notes for customers using legacy pin API.
clara: spike scheduled tomorrow: implement denylist O(1) lookup + tombstone_epoch guard. will post microbench numbers here.
maria: if anyone has a reproducible trace, paste it here. otherwise we'll run targeted canary after spike. :thumbsup:
